p: Because the ride itself is short, Thrill Coaster works best as part of a bigger outing. If you're heading to a gig or show at The O2, arrive a bit early and use it as a pre-show buzz. Families could pair it with a meal, a film or a wander round the outlet shops at the arena, making for an easy afternoon out.

A few tips. If you're nervous about VR, remember you can always close your eyes or lift the headset if it gets too much. Keep glasses on if you need them, as most headsets can accommodate them, and let the staff know if you need any help. Older children usually love it, but check the age and height guidance before you go.

For a bigger thrill after the virtual one, Up at The O2 lets you climb over the roof of the iconic dome on a walkway, with views across the Thames and Canary Wharf from the top. The cable car across the Thames runs from the Greenwich Peninsula to the Royal Docks, giving you a bird's-eye view of the river and the city.

Greenwich itself is a short hop away by bus or river boat, and is packed with things to do. The Cutty Sark, a restored 19th-century tea clipper, is a fantastic museum ship. Climb the hill in Greenwich Park to the Royal Observatory, where you can stand on the Prime Meridian line with one foot in each hemisphere. The National Maritime Museum, free to enter, is full of seafaring treasures, and Greenwich Market is great for food and crafts.
River boats stop at North Greenwich Pier, right next to The O2, so you can make a scenic trip of it, cruising down the Thames past the City of London.
